title: Revise burst accounting for mixed-reserved workloads and retroactive SLA adjustments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Tenants that run hybrid workloads (mix of reserved throughput and on-demand bursts across multiple pools) are being over-credited during regional failovers and when we retroactively apply SLA credits after partial pool degradations. We need a robust, auditable accounting model that: (1) attributes burst consumption and reserved throughput correctly at tenant level across pools and time, (2) supports retroactive SLA crediting without double-counting or violating usage quotas, and (3) provides clear reconciliation reports for finance and customers.
technical_summary: Introduce an event-sourced ledger for dedicated capacity usage that records per-request usage tokens, pool attribution tags, and an immutable credit/debit event stream. Implement a reconciliation pipeline that can (a) re-evaluate historical events for SLA credits, (b) generate compensating ledger entries rather than mutating past aggregates, and (c) apply tenant-facing accounting adjustments visible in billing exports. Key components: request shim to attach pool/reservation metadata, fast append-only event store (postgres append table + compacted Kafka topic), daily reconciliation job with windowed joins, prorated SLA credit calculator, and protective idempotency keys to prevent duplicate crediting during retries.
acceptance_criteria: Per-tenant hourly usage export shows reserved vs burst tokens with pool attribution for the last 90 days
Retroactive SLA credit run produces compensating ledger entries and a reconciliation report; verified by finance against sample incidents
No net double-crediting observed in synthetic replay tests across 10k tenants and simulated retries
End-to-end integration tests and load tests demonstrate <1% overhead on p50 request latency for accounting shim
Dashboard panel (billing console) exposes adjusted balance, credit history, and an explanation link for every tenant
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-17: Investigated previous incidents (INC-2026-14) where tenants saw unexpected SLA credits after region failover. Root cause: previous system mutated pre-aggregated counters during reconciliation, causing ambiguous history.

2026-02-20: Decided to use compensating ledger entries instead of backfilling aggregates. Trade-off: slightly larger storage and more complex reconciler logic vs. strong auditability and immutable history.

2026-02-24: Chose append-only Postgres table with Kafka mirror for replayability. Trade-off: increased ingest latency for analytics pipeline (mitigated by small real-time materialized view that powers billing exports).

2026-02-28: Rounding rules: usage tokens represented in micro-token units (1e-6) to avoid proration drift; SLA credits computed in micro-tokens and rounded down when presenting to customers, with remaining micro-tokens tracked in tenant-level carry-forward field.

2026-03-02: Idempotency design: every reconciler run must emit entries with reconciler-run-id and source-event-hash; duplicates are filtered by unique constraint on (source_event_hash, reconciler_run_id).

Decision to decouple quota enforcement from retroactive credits: quotas remain enforced on live aggregates; retroactive credits only produce billing adjustments and customer-facing balances, not runtime quota relaxations (avoids exposing windows where quota enforcement would be inconsistent).
implementation_tasks: Add pool attribution metadata to dispatcher request envelope and commit schema change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dispatcher/pull/987)
Create append-only ledger table and Kafka mirroring job (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/412)
Implement reconciler service that computes compensating entries (branch: billing/reconciler/mixed-reserved)
Add reconciliation CLI and scheduled job in airflow; include dry-run and audit modes
Instrument materialized view for hourly tenant export used by finance dashboard
Update billing exports schema and CSV format version to v3 and notify finance and customers
Implement idempotency unique constraints and backfill script for existing accounting rows
testing_and_validation: Unit tests for ledger write/read, idempotency and dedup logic
Integration tests that simulate pool failover and ensure compensating entries are produced once
Chaos test: simulate delayed reconciler runs and repeated retries; verify no duplicate credits
Synthetic load test: 10k tenants, 1M requests/day, validate accounting throughput and <5s tail latency for ledger writes
Reconciliation audit: compare reconciler output against gold dataset from finance team for 3 sample incidents (links in PR)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable ledger for 2 test tenants; run reconciler in dry-run and verify outputs (1 week)
Phase 2 (regional pilot): enable for 20 tenants in two regions, run daily reconciliations with audit, and expose corrections in billing console (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (global): enable for all dedicated pools, schedule backfill and reconcile historical windows in low-traffic weekend; monitor billing dashboard and finance signoff (planned weekend)
Emergency rollback: reconciler supports pause and compensating-void marker; revert UI exposure by toggling billing-export-version flag
